terms.definition: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager — a free AWS service that automates the creation, retention, copying, and deletion of EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs using lifecycle policies
terms.example: Like setting up an automatic backup schedule that never forgets and never leaves old backups piling up

terms.definition: A rule in DLM that defines which resources to target (by tag), when to create snapshots, how many to keep, and when to delete them
terms.example: A policy that says: every day at 2 AM, snapshot all volumes tagged Env=Production, keep the last 7

terms.definition: A point-in-time backup of an EBS volume, stored in Amazon S3 (managed by AWS), used for data recovery or volume duplication
terms.example: Like a photograph of your hard drive at a specific moment in time

terms.definition: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) where the root device is an EBS snapshot; can be used to launch identical EC2 instances
terms.example: A template built from a snapshot of a running server, used to spin up identical servers instantly

terms.definition: A snapshot that only stores blocks changed since the previous snapshot, reducing storage cost over time
terms.example: If your 100GB volume only had 5GB of new writes since last backup, only 5GB is stored in the new snapshot

terms.definition: The rule in a DLM policy that determines how many snapshots to keep or for how long before automatic deletion
terms.example: Keep the last 7 snapshots = delete the oldest when snapshot 8 is created

terms.definition: A retention mode in DLM that keeps exactly N snapshots and deletes the oldest when a new one exceeds the count
terms.example: Retain 5 → when snapshot 6 is created, snapshot 1 is automatically deleted

terms.definition: A retention mode in DLM that deletes snapshots older than a specified number of days, weeks, or months
terms.example: Delete snapshots older than 30 days — regardless of how many exist

terms.definition: A DLM feature that automatically copies newly created snapshots to a specified target AWS region for disaster recovery
terms.example: Snapshot created in ap-south-1 is automatically copied to us-east-1 for geo-redundancy

terms.definition: The mechanism DLM uses to identify which EBS volumes or instances to back up — by matching resource tags you specify in the policy
terms.example: Target all volumes with tag Backup=true — any new volume with that tag is automatically included

terms.definition: A DLM lifecycle policy where you manually configure all parameters — target tags, schedule, retention, copy rules, and tagging
terms.example: Used when you need specific schedules, retention counts, and cross-region copy settings

terms.definition: A DLM policy with pre-configured settings that automatically backs up all volumes or instances that do not have recent backups
terms.example: Quick setup with no configuration — AWS picks sensible defaults for you

terms.definition: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time — determines how frequently backups must be taken
terms.example: RPO of 4 hours = snapshots must run every 4 hours so you never lose more than 4 hours of data

terms.definition: The IAM role automatically created by AWS when you first create a DLM policy — grants DLM permission to create, describe, and delete snapshots
terms.example: Automatically assigned to your first DLM policy; no manual IAM setup required

terms.definition: An EBS feature (separate from DLM) that makes snapshots immutable — prevents deletion even by administrators, for compliance requirements
terms.example: Used together with DLM for regulated industries that require tamper-proof backups

terms.definition: The category of DLM policy — either EBS snapshot policy (for volume backups) or EBS-backed AMI policy (for creating AMIs)
terms.example: For backing up data volumes, choose EBS snapshot policy

terms.definition: The timing configuration within a DLM policy that defines when snapshots are created — can be fixed frequency (daily, weekly) or a custom cron expression
terms.example: Create a snapshot every day at 03:00 UTC using a daily schedule starting at that time

terms.definition: DLM is not part of the standard AWS Free Tier for compute — it is simply free as a service, always, regardless of tier
terms.example: You never pay for creating or running DLM policies, only for the snapshot storage they generate

terms.definition: The ability to restore data to exactly the state it was in at a specific past moment, using a snapshot taken at that time
terms.example: Restore your EBS volume to how it looked yesterday at 2 AM using the snapshot taken at that time

terms.definition: A syntax-based schedule format used in DLM for complex scheduling patterns not achievable with simple frequency settings
terms.example: cron(0 2 L * ?) = run at 2 AM on the last day of every month
